suite: SUIT — Sustainable University IT Infrastructure & Technology

scores.method: per-dimension 100 minus weighted deductions (CRITICAL -22, HIGH -9, MODERATE -3, LOW -1, INFO 0) over canonical post-merge findings; XCOH traceability sub-score reflects one unrealised obligation (charters) and one missing fallback against an otherwise verified F1-F6 obligation-to-mechanism matrix

findings.location: absent from O1.1-O8.1; absent from suit-solution/ch06-identity-EN.tex, ch07-policy-EN.tex, ch15-sizing-EN.tex; ch02-conceptual-frame-EN.tex:560-565 scopes out DR but not availability
findings.claim: No chapter or Q&A item addresses service availability of the self-operated critical planes: per-session policy-plane mediation makes identity and policy institution-wide single points of failure, yet the suite states no availability targets, no HA topology, and no fail-open/fail-closed semantics for PDP/IdP outage, and never engages the commercial-SLA comparison.
findings.fix: Add an availability/continuity section to the architectural-principles or sizing chapter (HA expectations per plane, PEP-side caching and token lifetime as PDP-outage mitigation, fail-mode policy per zone class) and a matching O-item in the solution argumentation module.

findings.location: absent from sections q-segmentation, q-autonomy, q-costs; absent from solution argumentation and ch28
findings.claim: Cyber-insurance underwriting conditions are never mentioned anywhere in the suite, although typical questionnaires (EDR everywhere, no unmanaged admin rights, perimeter inspection of all traffic) facially conflict with accountable researcher root access and the firewall-bypassing Science DMZ, giving a CISO a concrete unanswered refusal lever.
findings.fix: Add a Q-item in the policy module's costs-and-feasibility section answering the insurance objection: segmentation, MFA, observability and accountable root are the controls insurers reward; the Science DMZ's ACL+IDS profile is disclosable as a compensating control; charters give the insurer a named risk owner per zone.

findings.claim: Seven hardcoded cross-references to Chapter 5 are off by one after the insertion of section 5.2: replaceability-conditions pointers say 5.2 (actually 5.3) and standards-table pointers say 5.3 (actually 5.4).
findings.fix: Replace literal section-number strings with \S\ref{} to sec:ap-replaceability and sec:ap-standards; minimally bump every replaceability pointer to 5.3 and every standards-table pointer to 5.4.

findings.claim: The dossier's annotated ToC describes Ch.31 as a review of 15 named university IT architectures, but the canonical chapter is anonymized to role-based entries and names none of them.
findings.fix: Rewrite the Ch.31 annotated-ToC line to mirror ch31's anonymized section structure (European / North American / Asia-Pacific / Latin American precedent classes, regional research networks and consortium initiatives, documented gaps), removing the name list.

findings.claim: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690 is presented as the directly applicable technical baseline for NIS2 essential entities generally, although its Art. 1 scope covers only the digital-sector entity classes.
findings.fix: Rephrase: the Regulation details the Art. 21(2) families for the digital-sector entities in its Art. 1; for other essential entities (including universities) it is persuasive state-of-the-art guidance, with the binding baseline set by the national transposition.

findings.claim: The Researcher-LLM-API pilot says AI Act Art. 2(6) 'is typically invoked' for scoped commercial generative-AI API use — a misapplication of the research exemption that also directly contradicts the policy module's Q4.2, which states the exemption does NOT cover commercial-API use, handing a DPO the suite's own words as a refusal lever.
findings.fix: Replace the Art. 2(6) invocation in ch23 with the suite's canonical framing: risk-based classification with Art. 50 transparency for commercial APIs; Art. 2(6)/2(8) reserved for bespoke pre-market research tools.

findings.claim: A 2024 cyberattack with data theft is attributed to Sorbonne Université, while the cited source covers Université Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne (October 2024, ~73,000 directory records).
findings.fix: Rename the incident item to the institution the source covers, or replace the citation with a source documenting an incident at Sorbonne Université proper; do not alter the verified bib metadata.

findings.claim: The executive summary hard-codes 'pan-European' as a fixed attribute of the localized NREN key in three places, so any non-European edition renders jurisdictionally false prose (e.g. 'RNP and its pan-European backbone services').
findings.fix: Replace the three hard-coded 'pan-European (research) backbone' phrases with \loc{research-backbone-scale} (or a dedicated continental-backbone key with a generic Layer-0 default), letting EU archetypes rebind to 'the pan-European GEANT backbone'.

findings.claim: The solution-summary wrapper carries an inlined copy of the generic summary that no longer matches the current generic content: it misses the genericity-remediation changes, including the \loc{identity-federation-profile} consumption site, so the LU edition's bound RESTENA/eduGAIN value never renders and the retired 'brownfield Microsoft-centric' label plus unscoped EU instrument lists survive in the rendered edition.
findings.fix: Re-copy the current generic solution-summary content into the instance wrapper (keeping only the sanctioned \input{../set} localization delta), rebuild with latexmk -pdf, and refresh the rendered edition. Never edit the generic summary from the instance side.

findings.claim: Four Layer-0 keys consumed by the current generic title block via \suitmetablock (doc-version, doc-visibility, doc-approval-authority, doc-approval-date) are unbound in the LU set.tex; the Layer-0 default for doc-approval-date is the visible placeholder '(approval date to be set)', which will leak onto every LU title page once the wrappers are re-synced.
findings.fix: Bind the four keys in set.tex with the LU edition facts (e.g. \setloc{doc-version}{2.1}, \setloc{doc-visibility}{INTERNAL}, \setloc{doc-approval-authority}{\loc{approving-academic-units}}, \setloc{doc-approval-date}{May 7, 2026}), then re-sync the wrappers and rebuild.

findings.claim: Penn State Science DMZ case row swaps direction and mechanism: 'x5 to x12 gain' is stated as 250 Mbps sending / 600 Mbps receiving by 'bypassing' an RFC 1323-violating firewall, while the verified record gives ~5x inbound and ~12x outbound after the firewall's TCP-sequence-checking feature was disabled.
findings.fix: Align the table row with the verified bib record (esnet-pennstate): ~5x inbound / ~12x outbound, feature disabled not bypassed; drop or re-verify the 250/600 Mbps split.

findings.claim: UN HRC Resolution A/HRC/RES/47/16 is described as 'adopted by 43 votes to 0', an unsupported and likely false vote count; the verified record says adopted without a vote (by consensus), co-sponsored by some 70 states.
findings.fix: Replace 'adopted by 43 votes to 0' with 'adopted without a vote (by consensus), co-sponsored by some 70 states', or verify and cite the actual UN voting record.

findings.claim: Four instances over-attribute to the Verizon DBIR the claim that lateral movement in flat networks is a primary/dominant breach mechanism; the source documents credential theft and ransomware prevalence, while the lateral-movement control rationale belongs to NIST guidance.
findings.fix: Rephrase all four instances: attribute credential/ransomware prevalence to the DBIR and the segmentation-against-lateral-movement rationale to NIST SP 800-215 / SP 800-53 SC-7.

findings.claim: The anti-lock-in and conformance defences misname both canonical four-item sets they defend: O5.1's replaceability conditions and O6.1's conformance categories differ from the canonical names in ch05 and ch16 — exactly the 'self-graded exercise' impression O6.1 sets out to rebut, since a reviewer checking the chain of support finds the defending module disagreeing with the defended Reference.
findings.defectType: cross-document-drift (defence text drifts from canonical sets)
findings.fix: Align O5.1 and O6.1 wording to the canonical condition and category names (standard interfaces; open state/configuration formats; documented exit-data export; no hidden dependencies — and interface fidelity, data portability, exit rehearsal, decision auditability); the rebuttal logic survives unchanged.

findings.claim: The normative standards-landscape table labels vendor- or project-controlled artefacts as standards with inconsistent honesty: only the S3 row carries '(de facto standard)'; OPA REST, Cedar, DDM/DEP, MS-MDM, 'Declarative Linux config' and the CNI row (cited to Cilium, not the CNI specification) carry no qualifier, and the policy layer's lack of a standards-body interface (XACML) is not acknowledged the way the orchestration gap is.
findings.fix: Add the de-facto/vendor-specification qualifier to the affected rows, cite the containernetworking/cni specification for the CNI row, and add one sentence acknowledging the policy decision interface is a de facto project API with XACML as the deliberately non-adopted standards-body alternative.

findings.claim: The dossier's annotated ToC describes Ch.30 as a library of named vendor pairs (AD/Keycloak, SCCM/Ansible, Splunk/OpenSearch, VMware/K8s, NetApp/Ceph), but the canonical chapter titles every coexistence pattern role-based and names none of these products.
findings.fix: Replace the vendor-pair list with the six role-based pattern names used by ch30 and the solution-summary.

findings.claim: The synthesis chapter describes the suite as 'one of three documents' and claims the dossier reproduces this chapter as a technical-annex part — both statements no longer hold: the suite is four documents plus two Q&A modules, and the dossier carries a pointer/capsule part, not a reproduction.
findings.fix: Rewrite ch01 'Where this chapter sits in the suite' to the current composition: four-document suite (policy dossier with companion and Q&A part; technical reference with operational summary and Q&A module), with the dossier carrying a pointer/capsule of this Reference.

findings.claim: The Solution foreword claims the dossier includes 'an inspection report on deliverable quality' — no such document exists anywhere in the suite definition.
findings.fix: Drop the inspection-report clause from the foreword, or replace it with the regulatory-applicability annex and the operational summary, which do exist.

findings.claim: The synthesis wave-dependency figure omits three REQUIRED prerequisite edges declared by the canonical dependency table (2->5, 4->7, 1->8) while keeping the equally redundant 1->5; the figure's own source comments declare the full edge sets the drawing omits, so it matches neither the ch17 table nor a clean transitive reduction.
findings.fix: Draw the missing required edges in fig:synth-wave-dag, or apply a consistent transitive reduction (also dropping 1->5) and caption the figure as a reduced edge set with Table tab:pr-deps as the authoritative list.

findings.claim: The companion's 'concentric layers' view names only four of the five canonical structural layers (silently dropping exposed zones) and mis-attributes the model to the technical reference, whose model is the different nine-functional-layer architecture.
findings.fix: Add the exposed-zones layer (or an explicit elision note) and repoint the parenthetical to the main report's five-layer model (sec:concept-arch).

findings.location: companion-body-EN.tex:467; main-body-EN.tex:658-659; rendered summary is 8 pages
findings.claim: Hard-coded page counts drift in both directions: the main body calls the companion a 'four-page synthesis', the companion calls itself 'the present five-page document', and the rendered executive summary is 8 pages — with the companion sentence also rendered inside the dossier where the count is doubly wrong.
findings.fix: Use a count-free formulation in both places ('the accompanying executive summary' / 'the present executive summary'), which stays correct in both render contexts.

findings.claim: The orange clarificationbox carries opposite semantics in the two Q&A modules: 'insidious framing' (rhetorical-trap marker) in the policy module vs neutral 'clarification/disambiguation' in the solution module, violating the rule that the same colour means the same thing suite-wide.
findings.fix: Elect one orange-box semantics suite-wide (or introduce a distinct insidiousbox hue in the policy module), update both reader's guides, and re-tag divergent occurrences (e.g. Q1.3).

findings.location: main-body-EN.tex:4083-4097; token 'charter' absent from all suit-solution .tex
findings.claim: Policy obligation without a Solution mechanism: responsibility/enclave charters — load-bearing in Propositions P5 and P7, the companion's key messages and the federated-governance loop — are never realised, named or hooked anywhere in the Technical Reference.
findings.fix: Introduce 'zone responsibility charter' into ch08's zone-catalogue contract (each declared zone carries a charter with a named accountable owner) and into Wave-0/Wave-3 exit criteria; alternatively document in the Policy that the charter is realised by the Solution's zone-ownership and exception-register mechanisms.

findings.claim: Governing-board terminology is localization-routed in the companion (\loc{governing-board}) but hard-coded as literal 'top governing board' in the main report (6+ occurrences), so an instantiated edition renders the real board name in the summary but the generic phrase in the full report; the two documents also use different role names for the endorsement ladder.
findings.fix: Route the main report's 'top governing board' occurrences through \loc{governing-board}/\Loc{governing-board} and harmonise the deliberative-body role names between companion and main report.

findings.claim: Stricter Art. 23 incident reporting is presented as a consequence of essential (vs important) classification; the Art. 23 cadence is the same for both classes — the differential is supervision and sanctions.
findings.fix: Drop 'stricter incident reporting obligations (Article 23)' from the essential-entity differential, or recast as 'the same Article 23 reporting cadence as important entities, but under proactive supervision'.

findings.claim: The ten Art. 21(2) measure families are cited with national-transposition ordinal numbering (1\textdegree-10\textdegree) under a caption attributing them to the NIS2 Directive itself, whose points are lettered (a)-(j).
findings.fix: Convert the reference column (and line 4093) to NIS2 Art. 21(2)(a)-(j); if the national ordinal numbering is wanted, present it as a labelled worked-transposition column.

findings.claim: The data-classification tiers require a documented TIA only for identifying personal data, while pseudonymised personal data may be transferred under 'SCC + supplementary measures' with no TIA mentioned — understating the TIA duty that applies to all Art. 46-based transfers of personal data.
findings.fix: Add 'documented TIA' to the pseudonymised-data tier (SCC + TIA + supplementary measures), keeping the heavier consent/Art. 6 discussion for identifying data.

findings.claim: A public research-and-teaching institution is said to be 'typically classified' as a NIS2 essential entity on the basis of public-institution status — a national-transposition outcome overgeneralised as the typical cross-Member-State result.
findings.fix: Replace 'typically classified' with 'may be classified, depending on the national transposition', keeping the worked essential-entity pathway as the labelled example it already is.

findings.claim: States that 'research is not in itself a covered sector' under NIS2, while Annex II lists research organisations as a covered sector (important entities), with education establishments excluded by the Art. 6(41) definition.
findings.fix: Rephrase: research organisations are an Annex II sector (important entities), but the Art. 6(41) definition excludes education establishments, so universities usually enter scope by another route (public-administration designation, digital infrastructure, hospital affiliation), depending on the national transposition.

findings.claim: Third-country data egress is anchored on 'GDPR Art. 32 read with the Schrems II doctrine' — the security-of-processing article cited for the transfer regime, which is GDPR Chapter V (Arts. 44-49).
findings.fix: Replace with 'GDPR Chapter V (Arts. 44-49) read with the Schrems II doctrine' in both occurrences, matching the anchors used elsewhere in the same volume.

findings.claim: States 'NIS2 scope is a function of the service performed, not of headcount' and that self-operating network/identity/research-computing services brings an entity into scope irrespective of headcount — misstating the Art. 2(1) sector-and-size rule and treating internal self-provision as a scoping trigger.
findings.fix: Rephrase: where NIS2 captures an entity — by sector-and-size under Art. 2(1) or regardless of size under Art. 2(2) (e.g. public-administration designation) — its Art. 21/23 duties apply in full, without headcount-scaled relief; drop the claim that self-operated services trigger scope. (Preserves the ratified invariance message while correcting the legal mechanism.)

findings.claim: The board-decision economic case hangs its only sector-spend benchmark — security spend at 'roughly 8-15% of the IT budget' — on a citation (gartner-security-spend2024) that does not evidence the figure at the cited URL; if the benchmark falls, the quantitative frame drops below the suite's own three-layer convergence rule.
findings.fix: Re-anchor the figure to a source that actually states it (e.g. Gartner IT Key Metrics or an equivalent benchmark report) recorded in the entry note or as a separate bib entry, or reformulate the range as attributed to the EDUCAUSE/sector comparison only.

findings.claim: Per-institution 2025 Oracle EBS breach figures (University of Phoenix 3.5M records per SEC filing; Harvard 1.3 TB; Dartmouth 35,000+) are all cited to one aggregator entry whose metadata records none of these figures.
findings.fix: Record the per-institution figures in the entry's note with their primary anchors (SEC 8-K, institutional statements, attorney-general notice), or add those primary sources as separate bib entries cited alongside.

findings.claim: The main report states as universal fact that the adopter's NREN 'connects it to the European backbone GEANT', and the feasibility/cost case repeatedly grounds affordability on NREN/GEANT services as the adopter's own substrate — false as written for adopters outside the GEANT service area, with the cost rationale anchored on infrastructure they do not have.
findings.fix: Route the backbone through \loc{research-backbone-scale} or use the labelled pattern '(in Europe, GEANT; Internet2/ESnet, RedCLARA, UbuntuNet or APAN in other regions)'; in the cost sites say 'the NREN and its continental research backbone' keeping GEANT as a labelled example.

findings.location: all four render wrappers vs the current generic wrappers
findings.claim: The four instance wrappers no longer match the current generic wrappers despite their own keep-in-sync contract: they lack \usepackage{suit-logo}, \suittitlelogo, the \suitfootlogo footer and the \suitmetablock title block, and the policy wrapper's inlined Part V capsule — annotated 'reproduced here verbatim' — differs from the generic text (missing the five sovereignty-dimension parentheticals and the open-foundations product list).
findings.fix: Re-copy the current generic preambles/title pages into the four instance wrappers (retaining only the sanctioned \genericroot remap and \input{../set} addition), restore the verbatim Part V capsule, then rebuild all four documents with latexmk.

findings.claim: The geographic-origin line '(originally developed for the University of Luxembourg)' is hard-coded into ONE wrapper only, beyond the thin-shell contract, producing cross-document inconsistency within the edition; the content itself is legitimate for the LU instantiation — only the hard-coded single-document placement is the defect.
findings.fix: Move the origin clause into set.tex (fold into \setloc{author-affiliation} or a dedicated edition-note key consumed by all four wrappers), restore the wrapper to template form, and rebuild.

findings.location: O6.1, O8.1; ch16 Crypto exit test; ch13-crypto-EN.tex contract
findings.claim: No item pre-empts the objection that the Crypto layer's only exit-rehearsal test (HSM key migration preserving cryptographic identity) is unsatisfiable for non-exportable trust-anchor keys — common HSM best practice — making the Wave-1 exit gate potentially unpassable as designed.
findings.fix: State the wrap-export precondition in the Crypto contract and define the alternative exit artefact for non-exportable keys (planned key-rotation/re-anchoring rehearsal under dual control), then reference it from O6.1.

findings.claim: The collective labour-law prerequisite for workplace monitoring — consultation/co-determination of staff-representation bodies, which in several jurisdictions can block monitoring tools — appears nowhere: Q8.4 covers individual proportionality (Barbulescu) and the ICRADP gives staff a governance seat, but no Q&A item, wave precondition, or localization key covers the collective-consultation step that precedes lawful deployment of the observability pipeline.
findings.fix: Add a \loc{staff-representation-body} key and a sentence-level hook making staff-representation consultation a stated Wave-2/monitoring precondition where the adopter's labour law requires it, plus a short Q&A note under Q8.4.

findings.claim: GEANT backbone capacity given as 'multiple wavelengths at 400 Gbps' while the verified source description says speeds up to 500 Gbps.
findings.fix: Update to 'wavelengths of up to 400-500 Gbps' or 'up to 500 Gbps' per the verified record.

findings.claim: University of Florida row mis-attributes verified figures to phases: 'x20 from the first phase; scaling up to 200 Gbps' vs the record's 10x from the bandwidth upgrade, 20x once the Science DMZ was added, 200 Gbps for LHC/CMS data.
findings.fix: Reword the table row per the verified esnet-uflorida record.

findings.claim: 'Mean dwell time is the dominant cost driver' overstates what IBM Cost of a Data Breach 2024 supports.
findings.fix: Soften to 'breach lifecycle is a major cost driver: breaches contained faster cost measurably less (IBM 2024)'.

findings.claim: Seven institutional figures asserted beyond what the cited source records carry (MIT 100 Gbps backbone; Michigan among 34 Internet2 founders; EPFL ~12,000 students; Magna Charta 1,000+ signatories/94 countries; WLCG tier split; Paris-Saclay ransom non-payment; MOVEit victim-list extras).
findings.fix: For each, either enrich the bib entry with a verifying source that carries the figure, or hedge/drop the unverifiable specifics.

findings.claim: Named ISO 27001 university certifications (Leeds, Warwick, Eindhoven, plus 'various universities in Germany, Australia and Japan') carry no citations.
findings.fix: Add citations to published certification statements or certifier registries, or generalize with one verifiable example.

findings.claim: Claim that NGFWs achieve 100+ Gbps threat prevention but 'cost an order of magnitude more than the Science DMZ approach' closes on dart2013, which predates the hardware claim and carries no cost ratio.
findings.fix: Cite a current NGFW datasheet/benchmark plus a cost-comparison source, or soften to an unquantified trade-off keeping dart2013 only for the latency/state-tracking point.

findings.claim: 'University of Maryland (UMBC)' misnames the institution.
findings.fix: Rename to 'the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC)'.

findings.claim: The standards table attributes network access authentication AND accounting to RFC 2865 alone; accounting is RFC 2866, never cited.
findings.fix: Cite RFC 2866 alongside RFC 2865, or narrow the role text to authentication with accounting via the companion RFC 2866 family.

findings.claim: NFS v4.1 is anchored to RFC 5661, which was obsoleted by RFC 8881 (August 2020); a superseded document is cited as the current 'Stable' standard.
findings.fix: Re-point to RFC 8881 (or keep rfc-5661 with an 'obsoleted by RFC 8881' note) in the table, the ch10 contract, and the bib.

findings.claim: The standards-table caption defines exactly three status values (Stable, Mature, Emerging), but the OAuth 2.1 row uses an undefined fourth value 'Maturing'.
findings.fix: Change the row to 'Emerging' or add 'Maturing' to the legend with a one-line definition.

findings.claim: States MicroMDM/NanoMDM speak 'Apple's DDM/DEP protocols', overstating open-source Declarative Device Management support, which requires companion services and remains partial relative to commercial MDMs.
findings.fix: Reword to Apple's MDM protocol with DEP/ADE enrolment, and DDM where the chosen open server or companion components support it (coverage currently partial), keeping the honest-gap posture.

findings.claim: ch01 calls the second principal trajectory 'brownfield with a dominant proprietary productivity suite' while the canonical vocabulary is 'brownfield single-suite-centric'.
findings.fix: Use the canonical trajectory name at ch01:333, optionally keeping the paraphrase in parentheses on first use.

findings.claim: The observability reference stack is named three different ways across the suite (with/without Grafana, Loki vs Grafana Loki).
findings.fix: Pick one canonical rendering (the ch12 title plus 'Grafana Loki' for logs) and propagate it to the dossier capsule and the ch01 table.

findings.claim: The operational summary labels the sizing profile 'R-tier institution', a term appearing nowhere in the Technical Reference; ch15 says only 'research-intensive university' / 'reference profile'.
findings.fix: Rename to 'Sizing reference points (research-intensive reference profile)' and remove '(R-tier)', or introduce the tier nomenclature in ch15 first.

findings.claim: Four inline '(Part~\ref{part:reg-applicability})' references resolve via xr-hyper to a part of a different PDF without naming the target document, so the standalone reader sees a bare reference pointing outside the document in hand.
findings.fix: Qualify all four references, e.g. '(the Regulatory Applicability annex, Part~\ref{part:reg-applicability} of the complete dossier)'.

findings.claim: F2 instrument for an EU university given as NIS2 'with Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690' — a milder instance of the 2024/2690 scope overreach.
findings.fix: Qualify: '...with Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690 where the institution provides an in-scope digital service (otherwise persuasive technical reference)'.

findings.claim: Cites 2024/2690 as if its logging rules bind the institution.
findings.fix: Drop the eu-regulation-2024-2690 citation here or qualify it as the Commission's technical articulation for digital-sector entities, used by analogy.

findings.claim: 'NIS2 likewise attaches obligations to the function performed, not to headcount' — instance of the shared module's scoping-rule misstatement.
findings.fix: Mirror the corrected formulation adopted for LEG-8612a572: once in scope, NIS2 duties do not scale down with headcount; several scoping routes apply regardless of size.

findings.claim: NIS2 incident-reporting cadence given as '24 hours / 72 hours / 30 days (final report)' in three main-body sites, while the shared annex and the directive itself say one month.
findings.fix: Use '1 month' in all three main-body occurrences, matching the shared annex and NIS2 Art. 23(4).

findings.claim: 'NIS2 (2022, applicable since 17 October 2024)' conflates the transposition deadline with applicability.
findings.fix: Write '(2022, transposition deadline 17 October 2024; national measures apply from 18 October 2024)'.

findings.claim: A regular compliance/maturity report to competent authorities is stated as a direct directive consequence of essential-entity classification; it is a national-transposition mechanism reflecting Art. 32 supervision powers.
findings.fix: Add the qualifier '...where the national transposition so provides (as in the worked example), reflecting the directive's ex-ante supervision powers (Art. 32)'.

findings.claim: 'NIS2 Art. 21 (logging integrity)' is an imprecise provision anchor.
findings.fix: Cite 'NIS2 Art. 21(2)(b)/(f) (incident handling; effectiveness assessment)' instead.

findings.claim: One fetch_note of 299 carries no dated verification ('Working-group's own reference suite (self-reference).').
findings.fix: Append a dated note, e.g. 'repository URL confirmed June 2026'.

findings.claim: Proposition 6 (and the companion echo) justifies the open-source default by alignment with 'the European Commission's open-source strategy' — a local anchor used as a REASON for a universal proposition, unlabelled and without a substitution path for non-EU adopters.
findings.fix: Rephrase both sites: 'aligning with public-sector open-source strategies (e.g., the European Commission's open-source strategy in the EU)' — the e.g. label brings the anchor under the ratified labelled-example treatment.

findings.claim: Reference-panel criterion 2 asserts all panel institutions 'access the same NREN/GEANT backbone services' — factually inaccurate for the US members (Internet2/ESnet) and universalizing the EU backbone as the panel's common substrate.
findings.fix: Rephrase: equivalent NREN backbone services (GEANT in Europe, Internet2/ESnet in North America), interconnected into one global research fabric.

findings.claim: Proposition 10 unconditionally mandates federated identity via eduroam and the national identity federation, while the Technical Reference's identity contract provides the no-federation fallback the policy omits — undischargeable as written for adopters in countries without an operating federation.
findings.fix: Append the ch06 conditional: 'where a national identity federation operates; otherwise deploy the standards-based identity layer with interoperable federation metadata and defer participation (Technical Reference, Ch. 6)'.

findings.claim: The solution Q&A module's legal evidence layer names only EU instruments (GDPR, NIS2) without the worked-example label or \loc routing, while the policy-layer twin module carries the ratified labelled treatment.
findings.fix: Write 'binding legal and regulatory instruments of the adopter's jurisdiction (GDPR, NIS2 and sectoral law in the worked EU instantiation)' in the layer key, and route O3.1 through \loc{data-protection-regime}/\loc{cybersecurity-baseline-regime} with the '(in the EU, ...)' label.

findings.claim: The section-6 coverage note is stale and miscounted: it labels a 13-item list 'The 11 keys with a NEW consumption site' and declares as orphans six keys that now have real consumption sites in the generic suite (institution-type, data-protection-regime, cybersecurity-baseline-regime, identity-federation-profile, incumbent-identity-suite-vendor, research-backbone-scale); the keys render correctly, but the documented rationale no longer matches the suite.
findings.fix: Refresh the note: correct the count, move the six now-consumed keys out of the declared-orphan list, and keep the genuinely unconsumed keys with their why-comments.

findings.location: between O2.1 and O5.1 (natural slot for an O2.2)
findings.claim: No Q&A item assembles and rebuts the 'open source is itself the supply-chain/security risk' objection (unmaintained dependencies, no vendor CVE-response SLA, nobody to sue), although the answer's pieces exist across Q8.5, O5.1, Q9.4 and the sovereignty grid's Operational dimension.
findings.fix: Add a short O-item assembling the existing answers: commercial support subscriptions for open components, the supply-chain attestation control of Q8.5, and the grid's per-layer operational-sustainability scoring.

findings.claim: Gartner shadow-IT statistics (41% in 2022, projected 75% by 2027) are sourced to a vendor-blog compilation rather than the Gartner primary.
findings.fix: Optionally add the Gartner primary press-release URL to the bib entry's note; no prose change required.

findings.claim: Verification PASS record: the suite's headline quantitative claims check out against their verified source records.
findings.fix: None — recorded for baseline-diff continuity.

findings.claim: Verified sound: wave dependencies acyclic with full nine-layer test coverage; FTE envelopes nowhere summed and explicitly non-additive; conformance tests concrete and falsifiable with gaps openly acknowledged; reversibility/coexistence engineering-feasible; 9/3/10 counts consistent across all six documents; summary tables match ch15/ch17 exactly.
findings.fix: None — positive baseline for the next run's diff.

findings.claim: Verification record: the suite's core article-number and case-law-holding claims check out against the primary instruments.
